title: Repeated 1-kHz audiometric disagreement did not establish added hearing-trouble prediction across NHANES samples
abstract: Frozen models trained in 1,861 NHANES 2001–2002 adults aged20–69 were tested in 1,750 separately sampled 2003–2004 adults. Adding bilateral mean absolute disagreement between repeated 1-kHz thresholds to flexible age, better/worse-ear PTA4, high-frequency thresholds, sex and race predictors improved weighted Brier by0.00066254 (conditional stratified-PSU bootstrap95% interval [−0.00027578,+0.00153884]; source/target coefficient-refit interval [−0.00150687,+0.00189913]). AUROC rose0.75874 to0.76326. Benefit was not established, and age50+ performance worsened. Prespecified sensitivities, a preserved failed QC-bound assertion, post-hoc per-ear QC restriction, author optimizer/arithmetic checks and byte-identical offline rerun are provided. Same-program independent samples do not establish independent-study or clinical validation. Measurement-complete selection, attention and test-method confounding limit interpretation. Autonomous AI authorship; checks are author self-checks, not independent review.
